title: Refined Pfaffian Littlewood identity for spin Hall–Littlewood rational functions with nonzero gamma under uniform convergence bounds
author: Gavrilova, Svetlana
work: Refined Littlewood identity for spin Hall–Littlewood symmetric rational functions
difficulty_reason: The proof introduces a refined boundary vector, evaluates the infinite-spin partition function, establishes its symmetry and recursion, and proves a Pfaffian formula by polynomial-degree interpolation with a final normalization specialization. The full boundary and interpolation construction is retained; the infinite signature sum is justified by the stated uniform convergence bound.
source_scope_note: The selected problem is exact original Theorem1.1, gamma nonzero, t in(0,1), and the uniform admissibility restriction for every inhomogeneity. Complete author Sections1--4 retain all model definitions, deformed boundary vector/transfer-matrix argument, every Yang--Baxter relation/partition transformation, freezing/polynomial properties, full Pfaffian interpolation and terminal substitution; later specializations are unselected context. Primary statement and human proof are exact native author TeX. Thirty weight expressions and five reference-column function legends were originally supplied only in published figure-PDFs and are explicitly identified literal published-PDF transcriptions, separately editable here, not claimed as acquired native TeX. Original graph geometry is retained as licensed vector illustrations with exact panel/row/column source bindings. Native755 literal n-1,n hook-index wording remains unchanged beside the authored2n Pfaffian, last/second-last row multipliers and u_(2n-1),u_(2n) evaluation; no index correction or proof added. Three literal identity-one calls at169 use the approved strict1-only installed Noto U+1D7D9 renderer, with serif/stroke/width differences disclosed and original tensor exponents unchanged. Table formula row ordinary standalone font/size/grid presentation differs from the publisher; mathematical symbols and diagram-column correspondence are retained. All temporary builds/assets are not yet durably backed up.
